current_versions.rust: 1.99.0 stable, released 2026-10-01 (official Rust blog announcement re-fetched this pass); next is 1.100, not 2.0
current_versions.clippy: Ships as a rustup component versioned with the toolchain (1.99.0); guide's component pin tracks the toolchain
current_versions.rustfmt: Ships as a rustup component versioned with the toolchain; max_width 100 is its default target
current_versions.rust-analyzer: Official Rust language server (rust-lang/rust-analyzer), distributed as a rustup component; guide Sec.14 requires the pinned toolchain to drive it, but the Sec.2 template component list still omits it (proposal carried)
current_versions.miri: Nightly-only component; guide correctly treats it as an optional separate gate when the pinned nightly provides it
current_versions.debugger: No official Rust debugger; guide pairs the project's pinned toolchain for debugging (lldb/gdb via editor) - no stale named tool found

assertions_contracts.guide_position: assert! for established internal invariants (stays in release), debug_assert! for expensive redundant dev checks, never put required mutation inside an assertion, assertions never replace recoverable input validation.
assertions_contracts.best_practice: Matches std macro documentation: assert! is always active, debug_assert! is compiled out in release unless debug-assertions are enabled; the guide restates this accurately.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Fresh pass: guide Sec.5 text re-read and unchanged in substance; semantics unchanged through 1.99 (1.99.0 announcement re-fetched, no assertion-model change).

bounded_work.guide_position: Every loop, queue, retry, allocation and output carries a named bound with units; checked arithmetic before computing ends; explicit stack with depth cap instead of recursion over attacker-controlled depth.
bounded_work.best_practice: No official Rust source prescribes resource budgets (application policy, TigerBeetle/Power-of-Ten lineage); official docs do not contradict it, and std checked_* arithmetic is the documented mechanism the guide uses.
bounded_work.evidence: Stricter than mainstream by design, not contradicted. No std change through 1.99 removes or deprecates the checked arithmetic APIs relied on (1.99 announcement re-fetched this pass).

concurrency.guide_position: Bounded queues with a documented full-queue policy; documented lock ordering and protected invariant; never hold a blocking mutex across .await; own task handles; documented cancellation policy; generation tokens so stale completions cannot publish.
concurrency.best_practice: No official std/async guidance contradicts this; std documents dropping a future as cancellation without guaranteeing started external work stopped, exactly the guide's caution.
concurrency.evidence: Guide Sec.8 re-read fresh; async-cancellation text restates documented future-drop semantics accurately; nothing in 1.99 changes the async model.

error_handling.guide_position: Typed errors with bounded context for external/input failures, Option for legitimate absence, ? where the caller owns recovery, explicit match where failure changes cleanup/retry/state, no unwrap/expect on external data, I/O, locks or subprocess results, never silently discard a Result.
error_handling.best_practice: Current std documentation and idiom agree: Result/Option are the standard mechanisms, ? propagation and structured library errors remain the documented norm; nothing in 1.99 changes this.
error_handling.evidence: Guide Sec.5 re-read fresh; Rust 1.99 release notes (re-fetched) contain no error-handling model change.

formatting.guide_position: rustfmt is the mechanical authority; reviewed rustfmt.toml with edition 2024, max_width 100, 4-space tabs; ~70-line function review threshold.
formatting.best_practice: rustfmt remains the official formatter shipped with the toolchain; a small shared rustfmt.toml and a 100-column target remain standard practice. The 70-line rule is guide policy, not an official claim, and is labelled as such.
formatting.evidence: No rustfmt deprecation or replacement announced through Rust 1.99; rustfmt still listed among release components/changes in the re-fetched 1.99 announcement.

memory_ownership.guide_position: Borrow for inspection, own when retaining; clone() as explicit cost; forbid(unsafe_code) default; where unsafe is required, isolate it and deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn (full guide Sec.9, reworded in remediation item 13); local safety docs for every unsafe op; Miri as a gate. No Box::leak round-trip rule yet (proposal carried).
memory_ownership.best_practice: On the guide's edition-2024 baseline the unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn lint warns by default (explicit unsafe blocks inside unsafe fn are the edition default); denying it is a sound stricter elevation, which is what the remediated guide now does. Separately, 1.99 std documentation recommends against reclaiming memory obtained via Box::leak and similar leak functions, preferring Box::into_raw/into_non_null - a case the guide still does not address (proposal, not a stale claim).
memory_ownership.evidence: Remediation item 13 VERIFIED in current text: full guide Sec.9 now states the lint already warns by default on edition 2024 and that the guide denies it; the old 'consider' wording is gone from the full guide (it survives only in SKILL.md - see mechanical_fixes). Edition Guide page re-fetched this pass confirms warn-by-default. Rust 1.99 announcement (re-fetched) confirms the Box::leak documentation update.

security.guide_position: forbid(unsafe_code) default; build scripts/proc macros treated as executable trust; lockfile reviewed but not treated as safety proof; Command with separate argv, bounded/drained child output, deadlines, reaping; no secrets in argv or logs; handle-based path policy instead of string prefix checks; TLS verification on.
security.best_practice: Aligns with current official guidance (std Command does not invoke a shell on Linux; Child drop does not kill/wait - both restated accurately from std docs). No official source contradicts the stricter positions.
security.evidence: Guide Sec.10 re-read fresh and cites std Command and Child documentation directly for the two load-bearing claims; both remain accurate at 1.99.

static_analysis.guide_position: Compiler and Clippy warnings actionable, denied in gates (cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings); suppress single lints only at smallest scope with a reason; do not enable every pedantic lint then silence globally; Miri as separate gate for unsafe.
static_analysis.best_practice: Matches the Cargo/Clippy manual's documented invocation and the Clippy project's own CI guidance; Clippy still ships per-release with the toolchain (1.99 notes link its changelog).
static_analysis.evidence: Guide Sec.12 re-read fresh; it cites the Cargo manual cargo-clippy page directly and that invocation remains the documented one.

testing.guide_position: Boundary tests (zero, one, exact limit, limit+1, overflow, cancellation, stale completion, failure before commit), property tests and fuzzing where the input space warrants, hermetic vs external tests separated, feature matrix tested explicitly, gates: fmt check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test debug and release with --locked.
testing.best_practice: Consistent with Cargo book guidance on test organization and profile differences; the debug+release double run is stricter than default practice but not contradicted.
testing.evidence: Gate commands re-read fresh use only documented Cargo/Clippy flags; no flag used by the guide was removed through 1.99.

toolchain_pins.guide_position: Pin an exact reviewed nightly date in rust-toolchain.toml (template channel nightly-YYYY-MM-DD, components rustfmt/clippy/rust-src); record active toolchain on disagreement; Sec.16 validation record now states the reference module was compiled with Rust 1.99.0, edition 2024, warnings denied, six tests passing in debug and -O (remediation item 14). Header still reads 'Document reviewed 2026-09-20'.
toolchain_pins.best_practice: The pinning mechanism (rustup toolchain files and override rules) is current and correctly described, and current stable is 1.99.0 (2026-10-01). The guide's recorded validation evidence now matches that current toolchain because item 14 re-ran the Sec.16 recipe under rustc 1.99.0 rather than re-typing the version line.
toolchain_pins.evidence: Remediation item 14 VERIFIED in current text: Sec.16 validation record names Rust 1.99.0 (the 1.90.0 line is gone). Rust 1.99.0 announcement re-fetched this pass (dated 2026-10-01). The rust-analyzer template omission is unchanged and remains a proposal, not a stale claim.

mechanical_fixes.correct: deny `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` (on edition 2024 it already warns by default; this guide denies it), matching the remediated full guide Sec.9
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Remediation item 13 reworded the full guide (references/TIGER_STYLE_RUST.md Sec.9) but the SKILL.md operational core still carries the pre-remediation 'consider' wording, so the two files now disagree on strength; SKILL.md itself says the full guide wins, but the summary should not understate the rule.

proposals.proposal: Add rust-analyzer to the rust-toolchain.toml template component list (or state explicitly that it is installed outside the pin). Section 14 requires the project's selected toolchain to drive rust-analyzer, checks, formatting and debugging alike, but the Section 2 template components list contains only rustfmt, clippy and rust-src, so a project copied from the template does not get a pinned rust-analyzer. Carried forward from run 1: facts unchanged, adoption still not applied.
proposals.evidence: rust-analyzer is the official Rust language server and is distributed as a rustup component, so it can be pinned in the same file; template re-read fresh in this pass and still omits it.
proposals.recommendation: Add "rust-analyzer" to the template components and note that per-project opt-out is fine where the editor manages it.

proposals.proposal: Add a leak rule: memory produced by Box::leak (and the other std leak functions) must not later be reclaimed/deallocated via a round-trip conversion; use Box::into_raw / Box::into_non_null where later reclamation is part of the contract. Carried forward from run 1: the 1.99 fact is confirmed, adoption still not applied (no Box::leak rule exists in the current guide text).
proposals.evidence: Rust 1.99 updated the std documentation for Box::leak to recommend against round-trip unleaking because of interactions with current and future compiler optimizations and the upcoming custom-allocator stabilization, and says the same guidance applies to the other std leak functions (announcement section re-fetched this pass).
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a one-line ownership rule with an adversarial test on any wrapper that leaks.
